questions.stem: Using Source D and Source G, give TWO reasons why it is important to protect ecosystems on Aogashima Island.
questions.stimulus: Refer to pages 2–3 of the Stimulus Booklet to answer parts (a)–(c).

criteria.text: Provides TWO reasons why it is important to protect ecosystems with reference to the information provided
Outlines why it is important to protect ecosystems on Aogashima Island
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: Utility value is the ability of ecosystems to satisfy the economic wants of humans. This island is home to endangered birds and would attract birdwatchers as tourists to visit and boost the island’s economy. The fact some species of birds are endangered also means it is important they are protected from human impacts, such as road use, to maintain genetic diversity.

questions.sampleAnswer: A biogeographical process shown is succession. As shown in the diagram, this involves lava hardening to form a new surface. Lichen carried by wind initially help to build up the soil. As more soil forms and can hold water, larger plants can grow and over many years a mature community is established.

questions.stem: Describe internal linkages between people in ONE economic enterprise operating at a local scale.

Demonstrates a sound understanding of internal linkages between people in the economic enterprise
Demonstrates an understanding of linkages in the economic enterprise

questions.sampleAnswer:
Economic enterprise: The River Oyster Shed

Pete is the owner and main link to the other employees at The River Oyster Shed. Andrew works for Pete three days a week; Pete and Andrew sometimes share looking after different oyster beds and sometimes do larger projects like oyster processing together. Deb works in retail at the shed sometimes, receiving and selling harvested oysters from Pete and Andrew.

questions.stem: How has ONE market preference changed the nature of the economic activity?
questions.stimulus: Answer parts (b)–(c) with reference to an economic activity you have studied.

criteria.text: Provides cause and effect for how a market preference has changed the nature of the named economic activity
Shows understanding of a market preference and the changed nature of an economic activity
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer:
Economic activity: Viticulture

Preference for red wines in China has led to wine producing regions growing more grapes for red wines, for example Australian wine companies during the 2010s increased their production of red wine grape varietals such as shiraz and cabernet sauvignon and built their marketing efforts (including social media campaigns) towards China.

questions.stem: Discuss the social impacts of the economic activity.
questions.stimulus: Answer parts (b)–(c) with reference to an economic activity you have studied.

criteria.text: Demonstrates a comprehensive understanding of the social impacts of the named economic activity
Demonstrates a thorough understanding of the social impacts of the named economic activity
Demonstrates a sound understanding of the social impacts of an economic activity
Demonstrates some understanding of the impacts of an economic activity/enterprise
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: Wine making leads to a range of good and bad social impacts. Wine is a positive part of many cultures around the world, providing joy and happiness to many, in consuming wine and also visiting wineries. However, it also leads to social problems such as alcoholism and high crime rates. Wine making provides strong identity and livelihoods, including through tourism for many regions such as the Hunter Valley. It can leave communities economically exposed though, during industry down cycles such as during the 2021 trade tensions with China.

questions.stem: Describe ONE way that the operation of global networks can influence the role of world cities.

criteria.text: Describes ONE way global networks can influence the role of world cities
Outlines ONE way global networks could influence the role of world cities
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: Global networks allow world cities to show economic authority by connecting them to each other and other urban centres, as they are the key nodes on the global communication network. Having this position allows cities such as New York to host major companies as they can use the network connections to communicate business decisions around their region and the world.

questions.stem: How has ONE urban dynamic of change influenced the location of residential land in a large city of the developed world?

criteria.text: Demonstrates an extensive understanding of how ONE urban dynamic of change influenced the location of residential land in a large city of the developed world
Demonstrates a sound understanding of the location of residential land and may make reference to an urban dynamic
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: The urban dynamic of urban consolidation results in high density residential land being located closer to key business and commercial hubs and key infrastructure in Sydney. This can occur in previous brownfield sites used for commercial or industrial purposes such as at Castle Hill Showground where apartment buildings replace low density housing and commercial/industrial land.

questions.stem: Using Source C on page 1 of the Stimulus Booklet and the extract, account for the changing role of regional centres.
questions.stimulus:
An extract from a 2016 Australian Parliamentary report is shown.
“Regional capitals serve as hubs for larger regional areas. They provide their own communities and those in smaller surrounding communities access to education, jobs . . . opportunities for cultural participation along with a host of other amenities that are essential to support strong and vibrant communities . . .”
© Australian Government

criteria.text: Demonstrates comprehensive understanding of reasons for the changing role of regional centres with clear links to the stimulus
Demonstrates a thorough understanding of reasons for the changing role of regional centres linked to the stimulus
Demonstrates a sound understanding of the changing role of regional centres and may reference the stimulus
Demonstrates some understanding of regional centres and/or their role
Provides some relevant information

questions.sampleAnswer: Regional centres share key infrastructure and services such as the provision of education through University Hubs which draw in residents from the wider area. They are also absorbing residents who are leaving small towns as they have a lack of investment and people to sustain the local economy. This has led to the demise of key services in small towns, resulting in a further changing role of regional centres to provide this for their regions. Regional centres also enable a higher quality of services and access to jobs, shown by RUN jobs increasing to 11 300 from 2015 to 2018 (Source C) as resources are pooled to provide support for the larger regional area as shown in the quote.
